pairs.subject: background-jobs
pairs.evidence: src/api/pipeline/workflows.ts:15 cancelWorkflowJob resolves void while the backend writes the terminal state at once as Failed (src-tauri/src/background_job.rs:684) and the WorkflowJob projection omits cancel_outcome (src-tauri/src/commands/infrastructure/workflows.rs:18), so no caller can show cancelling or tell cancelled from failed

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/src/background_job.rs:684 cancel() jumps straight to JobStatus::Failed with no cancelling state; src-tauri/src/commands/infrastructure/workflows.rs:66 folds cancelled jobs into failed_count, collapsing cancelled and failed into one endpoint; the snapshot field that would separate them (src-tauri/src/background_job.rs:221 cancel_outcome) is dropped by the projection at src-tauri/src/commands/infrastructure/workflows.rs:18 despite the command's own doc promising it at :134
not judged: the supervisor lives in src-tauri/src/background_job.rs, which is outside this API-wrapper context
not judged: tick bodies are backend code outside this context
not judged: no polling cadence lives in src/api/pipeline/
not judged: src/api/pipeline/scheduler.ts:13 exposes getSchedulerStatus but the health surface itself is backend code
not judged: src/api/pipeline/scheduler.ts:40 wraps missed-run listing, but the sweep and its policy belong to scheduling and the backend

pairs.registryProposal: Coverage gap on the consumer side, not a corpus hole: the repo's actual background runtime (src-tauri/src/background_job.rs - BackgroundJobManager, CancelOutcome, spawn_guarded) appears in no context of context-map.json, so background-jobs is paired only with an IPC-wrapper context and loop-supervision/tick-isolation/loop-health-telemetry can never be judged here. Also: src/api/pipeline/workflows.ts has zero importers in src/ and its WorkflowJob/WorkflowsOverview bindings are orphan-allowlisted (no TS derive), so the deviation is latent - the first UI wired to this API inherits it.
